---
title: Playground
icon: FlaskConical
description: Run Wakaru in your browser. Nothing to install, and no code leaves your machine.
---

Use the [playground](https://wakarujs.com/playground/) to see what Wakaru
can recover, compare settings, or share a small example. It runs the same
engine as the CLI in your browser. Your code is processed locally, with
nothing to install or upload.

![The playground: minified input on the left, decompiled JavaScript on the right](/screenshots/playground.png)

## Read minified code

Paste JavaScript into the left pane in **Decompile** mode. Readable output
appears on the right and updates as you edit. If you do not have a file
handy, choose a sample from **Example**.

Start with the default **Standard** level. Switch to **Minimal** to stay
closer to the input's behavior, or **Aggressive** to try further recovery.
See [Rewrite levels](/guides/rewrite-levels) for an example of the difference.

The playground also formats the result by default. If you are comparing
it with CLI output, turn off **Formatter** or add `--formatter` to your CLI
command. Warnings appear below the output.

## See what survives a round trip

Want to see how well Wakaru restores a particular JavaScript pattern?
Choose **Compile & Restore** and write modern JavaScript or JSX on the
left. Pick Babel, SWC, or esbuild under **Producer**. The playground compiles
your code, then passes that output to Wakaru.

You can inspect all three versions: your source, the compiled code, and
the restored result. Open **Diff** to compare the result with what you
wrote. Try changing a condition or JSX expression and watch how the
compiled and restored versions respond.

![Compile & Restore: original source, Babel output, and the Diff tab comparing Wakaru's output against the original](/screenshots/roundtrip-diff.png)

## Trace a change back to the input

Turn on **Mapping** when you want to see where recovered code came from.
Mapped output lines are colored by their input line. Hover a line on
either side to highlight the corresponding code on the other.

![Mapping view: each output line colored by its input line, with a hovered pair connected by an arrow](/screenshots/mapping.png)

Mapping turns off the formatter to keep those positions aligned. The
percentage beside the switch shows how much of the output has a mapping.
See [Source maps](/guides/source-maps) to save mappings with the CLI.

## Read a Vue component

For compiled Vue 3 code, turn on **Vue SFC** to try recovering a template
and setup code. When recovery succeeds, a **Vue SFC** tab appears beside
the JavaScript output, so you can compare both views of the component.

This is experimental. If recovery is not possible, the JavaScript output
remains available. See [Vue SFC](/guides/vue-sfc) for an example and what
can be recovered.

## Share an example

Click **Share** to copy a link with your code and settings. Someone else
can open it and continue from the same example, which is useful for
discussing a result or reporting a bug.

The code is stored in the link itself. Anyone with the link can read it.
If the input is too large to share, the playground tells you. For bug
reports, include the engine version and commit shown in the header too.

## When to use the CLI instead

Use the CLI to [unpack bundles](/guides/unpack-a-bundle), process multiple
files, or [apply an input source map](/guides/source-maps). It is also the
better fit for large inputs and scripted workflows.

See [Quick Start](/) for the first commands.
